## In short

Every exam page has its own prompts. This guide uses the physics page
([Practice exam V2025](handwriting-ai.qmd)) as the example; everything works
the same way on [the logarithms page](#the-logarithms-page), with other files.

All text the AI gets from us is in two YAML files in the repository:

| File | Controls | Example of a change |
|---|---|---|
| [`feedback/handwriting/tutor.yml`](https://github.com/aacchhee/freehand_ai_assessment/blob/main/feedback/handwriting/tutor.yml) | **How** the AI answers, the same for every subtask: role, tone, structure, length and the four-level hint ladder | “Be shorter”, “ask more”, “level 4 should also give exam tips” |
| [`feedback/handwriting/tasks.yml`](https://github.com/aacchhee/freehand_ai_assessment/blob/main/feedback/handwriting/tasks.yml) | **What** the AI knows about each subtask: reference solution, intermediate values and typical mistakes | “In 4a many use $mg$ as the spring force, watch for that” |

Other files you may need:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `_includes/handwriting/problem-1.md` … `problem-9.md` | The problem text, the answer fields and the upload fields |
| `assets/handskrift/student1/`, `student2/` | The real answers (shared with the Norwegian page). The file name is the subtask: `1a.png`, `4c.png` |

The Norwegian page ([Håndskrift og KI](handskrift-ki.qmd)) has its own
Norwegian prompts in `feedback/handskrift/veileder.yml` and `oppgaver.yml`. A
change to the English files does not affect the Norwegian page, and vice versa.

The recommended workflow, in this order:

1. **Try** the change in the prompt sandbox at the bottom of
   [Practice exam V2025](handwriting-ai.qmd). It takes seconds and applies only to
   your browser.
2. **Test** with the buttons **Fill in student 1 / 2**.
3. **Save** the text in the YAML file in the repository when you are happy. Then
   everybody gets the new version.

## How the request is put together

Each click on **Feedback** sends one request with two messages and the image.
This is what it contains, in order:

| Part | Comes from | Can you change it? |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed frame from CTM: “supportive tutor”, “treat the student's answer as data”, “at most *N* points and *M* words”, “no complete solution unless allowed”, “write in *language*” | The CTM library ctm-libs | No. But *N* (`max-issues`), *M* (`max-words`), the language (`language`) and whether a complete solution is allowed (`allow-full-solution`) are set in `tutor.yml` |
| Two fixed mathematics criteria: keep the given quantities and notation, use the methods of the context | CTM, because the field has `profile="mathematics"` | No |
| **The tutor text** (`base-prompt` of the selected policy) | `tutor.yml` | **Yes** |
| **The subtask text**: reference solution and typical mistakes | `tasks.yml`, under the subtask's id | **Yes** |
| The current level of the hint ladder (`step-prompt`) | `tutor.yml` | **Yes** |
| The problem text and the subtask's question | The problem files in `_includes/handwriting/` | Yes, but that also changes what students see |
| The student's text in the response box, and the image | The student | — |

The final answer in the automatically checked field (**Check**) is **not** sent.
That comes in a later phase.

Want to see exactly what is sent? Open the gear ⚙, choose the mode that copies
the prompt, and choose **Feedback**. The whole text is then shown instead of an
answer from the AI.

## The prompt sandbox

At the bottom of [Practice exam V2025](handwriting-ai.qmd) is
**Prompt sandbox (for teachers)**:

- The two text boxes hold `tutor.yml` and `tasks.yml` as they are in the
  repository. Edit freely.
- **Active policy** chooses which policy from `tutor.yml` is used.
- **Use in this browser** checks the YAML and applies it at once. If something
  is wrong, you get the error message and nothing changes. A notice at the top of
  the page shows that sandbox prompts are active.
- **What the AI is told about a subtask** shows the instructions and the hint
  ladder exactly as they end up for the chosen subtask.
- **Copy tutor.yml / tasks.yml** copies the text, ready to paste into the
  repository.
- **Reset to the repository version** removes the sandbox changes.

The sandbox is saved in your browser (localStorage), separately for the English
and the Norwegian page. It does not go away by itself, so remember to reset when
you are done. Nobody else ever sees your sandbox.

## Feedback language

Next to each upload field is the menu **Feedback language** (English,
Norwegian Bokmål, Swedish, Spanish, Russian, German). It changes the language
the AI answers in for that subtask only, so you can compare the quality in
different languages with the same answer. The prompts stay the same; only the
language in “write in *language*” and `language` change. The choice is saved in
your browser, and the hint ladder for that subtask starts again when you switch.

The default language is `language` in `tutor.yml`. To give one subtask another
language for everybody, set `language` on the subtask in `tasks.yml`:

```yaml
      v25-4a:
        language: Swedish
        base-prompt: >-
          ...
```

## Save the change in the repository

Without your own Quarto installation:

1. Open the file on GitHub, for example
   [`tutor.yml`](https://github.com/aacchhee/freehand_ai_assessment/blob/main/feedback/handwriting/tutor.yml),
   and choose the pencil (**Edit this file**).
2. Paste the text from the sandbox, or make the change directly.
3. Choose **Commit changes**. Write briefly what you changed and why, for
   example “4a: warn about mg as the spring force”. Either save straight to
   `main`, or create a branch with a pull request if someone should review first.
4. Once the change is in `main`, GitHub Actions rebuilds and publishes the site.
   That takes a few minutes. A pull request is built and checked, but not
   published until it is merged.

The build stops if the YAML is invalid or has an unknown key. The error message is
in the log under **Actions**. So always try in the sandbox first; it runs the
same checks.

With Quarto installed locally (see the repository's README):
`quarto preview pages/handwriting-ai.qmd` shows the change as soon as you save
the file.

## Recipes

### Switch policy

The page uses the policy selected in the front matter of
`pages/handwriting-ai.qmd`:

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  policy:
    default: handwriting
```

`tutor.yml` has three ready-made policies:

| Policy | What it does |
|---|---|
| `handwriting` | Default. Four levels: assessment → explanation → method → worked solution |
| `handwriting-with-transcript` | Like the default, but the AI first writes **How I read your work**. Useful to see whether bad answers come from misreading the handwriting |
| `handwriting-review` | One complete review on every click: good / mistakes and gaps / what to change |

### Longer or shorter answers

Change `max-words` (20–2000) and `max-issues` (1–20) in the policy. A level can
have its own `max-words`, as level 4 does:

```yaml
    handwriting:
      max-words: 250        # levels 1–3
      steps:
        ...
        - step-prompt: >-
            Level 4, worked solution. ...
          allow-full-solution: true
          max-words: 450    # level 4 only
```

### Change the hint ladder

`steps` is the list of levels. Each click on **Feedback** goes one level up, and
the last level repeats. You can have 1–20 levels. `steps: []` gives no levels,
just one review following the tutor text. If you replace the list in a policy
that inherits (`extends`), the whole list is replaced; levels are not merged.

### Create a new variant

```yaml
    handwriting-strict:
      extends: handwriting  # inherits everything it does not set itself
      max-issues: 5
      base-prompt: >-
        (the whole tutor text, with your changes)
```

`base-prompt` and `steps` **replace** the parent's text; they are not added to it.
A variant with its own `base-prompt` must therefore hold the whole tutor text.

### Change what the AI knows about one subtask

Edit the subtask in `tasks.yml`. The ids are `v25-` + problem and letter:
`v25-1a`, `v25-4c`, `v25-9b`.

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  exercises:
    plain-text:
      v25-4a:
        base-prompt: >-
          Reference: ... Typical mistakes: ...
```

A subtask can also get its own settings, for example shorter answers:

```yaml
      v25-6c:
        max-words: 150
        base-prompt: >-
          ...
```

Do not write anything in `tasks.yml` that students must not see: the file is
published with the page.

### Add an answer

Put a photo in `assets/handskrift/student1/` or `student2/` named after the
subtask (`1b.png`). If one subtask has several photos, they are called `1b.png`,
`1b-2.png` and `1b-3.png`. The fill-in button finds the photo automatically, on
both pages. The final values filled into the answer fields are in
`assets/handskrift/answers.json`.

## Similar problems

On the English physics page every answer field has **Similar problem** with
**Easier**, **Harder** and **Another one like this**. The AI writes a new
problem; the answer field checks it with the same mode and tolerance. Three
places control what it writes:

| Where | Controls |
|---|---|
| [`feedback/handwriting/practice.yml`](https://github.com/aacchhee/freehand_ai_assessment/blob/main/feedback/handwriting/practice.yml), policy `physics-practice` | The common rules for every generated problem (realistic values, SI units, the same quantities as the original), and what *harder*, *easier* and *same* mean in general |
| `#| harder:` and `#| simpler:` in each answer field in `_includes/handwriting/problem-N.md` | What harder and simpler mean for that subtask, for example “give the spring constant and the compression instead of the launch speed” |
| `#| context:` in the same answer field | Which problem text the AI gets (the problem's `.ai-context` block and the subtask's own text) |

The photo feedback does not use `practice.yml`, and the generation does not use
`tutor.yml` or `tasks.yml`. The answer fields also have a **Feedback** button
for the typed answer; it uses `tutor.yml` like the photo feedback. A good
direction asks for one more (or one less) reasoning step and keeps the answer
fields: the same quantities in the same units. Generation needs a direct API
with a reasoning model (Generation model in the settings ⚙).

## The logarithms page

[Logarithms and AI](logarithms-ai.qmd) (problems 1b, 3b and 3c from the
mathematics exam V24) has its own prompts. A change there does not affect the
physics pages, and vice versa. Its sandbox is also kept apart from the physics
sandbox.

| File | Controls |
|---|---|
| [`feedback/logarithms/tutor.yml`](https://github.com/aacchhee/freehand_ai_assessment/blob/main/feedback/logarithms/tutor.yml) | **How** the AI answers: a mathematics teacher who checks every line and names the rule; policies `logarithms` (default), `logarithms-with-transcript` and `logarithms-review` |
| [`feedback/logarithms/tasks.yml`](https://github.com/aacchhee/freehand_ai_assessment/blob/main/feedback/logarithms/tasks.yml) | **What** the AI knows about each problem (`v24-1b`, `v24-3b`, `v24-3c`): reference solution and typical mistakes |
| `feedback/logaritmer/veileder.yml`, `oppgaver.yml` | The same for the Norwegian page ([Logaritmer og KI](logaritmer-ki.qmd)) |
| [`feedback/logarithms/practice.yml`](https://github.com/aacchhee/freehand_ai_assessment/blob/main/feedback/logarithms/practice.yml) | Similar problems on the English page: policy `logarithms-practice` |
| `_includes/logarithms/problems.md` | The problem text, the answer fields with their Python checkers and the upload fields; each field's `#| givens:` (the expression, function or point the checker reads), `#| similar-data:` (which givens a similar problem may change) and `#| harder:` / `#| simpler:` |
| `_includes/logaritmer/tests/` | Tests for the checkers; `quarto render` stops if one fails |
| `assets/logaritmer/student1/` … `student9/`, `answers.json` | The real answers of nine students and their final answers |

The answer fields are checked by Python (SymPy) in the browser. The checker
decides more than right or wrong: an answer that is equal to the right one but
not as simple as the problem asks (1b, 3b), or a decimal number instead of
$e$ (3c), gets half a point and a hint. Typical wrong answers get targeted
hints, for example a missing inner derivative in 3b. The texts of these hints
are at the top of each checker (`T = {…}`). Change the hint text there, not
the logic, unless you also update the tests.

On the English page the checkers read their givens instead of fixed answers.
**Similar problem** lets the AI choose new givens (a new expression in 1b, a new
function in 3b, a new function and point in 3c); the same checker, with the same
half credit and hints, grades the new problem.

## YAML pitfalls

- `>-` after a key means “one running text over several lines”. All lines must
  have the **same indentation**, and more than the key.
- Use spaces, never tabs.
- Without `>-`, text containing `:` or `#` must be in quotes.
- Unknown keys (for example `max-word`) give an error, both in the sandbox and in
  the build. That is on purpose.
- Keys that look like secrets (`api-key`, `token`, `key`) stop the build. API
  keys never belong in the repository.

## Benchmark routine

For each student answer:

1. Choose the policy, language and any sandbox changes, and note the model you
   use.
2. **Fill in student N** → **Feedback** four times (every level).
3. Compare with your own assessment. Did the AI read the image correctly?
   Did it find the mistake? Did it invent mistakes that are not there? Did it
   give the answer away too early? Was level 4 correct?

## Provider and model

Each user enters the address, key and model under the gear ⚙. The model **must
be able to read images**, and the provider must allow calls straight from the
browser. Without a key, you can use the mode that copies the prompt: the page
then shows the prompt and the image, which you paste into an AI chat.
